# noindex

*Directive*

A robots meta tag or X-Robots-Tag rule that tells Google not to show a page in search results.

**Glossary** (*noindex*): A robots rule that tells Google not to show a page in search results. It works only if Google can crawl the page and see the rule.

Narrative: the topic [Robots meta tags and noindex](../topics/robots-meta-tag.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

29 claims mention it: 7 from Google's documentation, 14 shown or said at the event (3 not in Google docs, 4 confirmed by Google docs, 6 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 8 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Block Search indexing with noindex](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/block-indexing), [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag).

- [`D1-C109`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Docs: Google advises against using noindex to save crawl budget and against using robots.txt to temporarily reallocate budget. Use robots.txt only for pages you never want crawled, and 404 or 410 for removed pages. `[D1-C109, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawl-budget]`
- [`D2-C022`](../sessions/D2-S02-welcome-to-indexing-day.md) Docs: Google's noindex documentation says the noindex rule works only if the page is not blocked by robots.txt: a crawler that cannot fetch the page never sees the rule, and the page can still appear in search results, for example if other pages link to it. `[D2-C022, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/block-indexing]`
- [`D2-C854`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Docs: Google's JavaScript SEO basics guide says that when Google encounters a noindex rule it may skip rendering and JavaScript execution, so using JavaScript to change or remove a noindex robots meta tag may not work as expected. `[D2-C854, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics]`
- [`D2-C192`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Docs: Google's JavaScript guides say that when client-side routing makes a real 404 status impractical, a single-page app can avoid soft 404s by redirecting with JavaScript to a URL whose server returns 404, or by adding a robots noindex meta tag with JavaScript. `[D2-C192, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics]`
- [`D2-C294`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Docs: For client-side rendered single-page apps, where meaningful status codes can be impossible or impractical, Google's documentation gives two ways to avoid soft 404s: a JavaScript redirect to a URL that returns a 404 status, or a noindex robots meta tag added with JavaScript. `[D2-C294, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics]`
- [`D2-C529`](../sessions/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) Docs: Google's documented ways to keep a site's images out of search results are a robots.txt disallow rule (for example for Googlebot-Image) or a noindex X-Robots-Tag HTTP header, with the Removals tool for emergencies. `[D2-C529, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/prevent-images-on-your-page]`
- [`D3-C673`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Docs: Google's Removals tool help says a temporary removal request usually takes up to a day to process and lasts only about six months, so the content must also be removed permanently, for example with a 404 or 410, a noindex or a password. `[D3-C673, docs, Google Search Console Help, https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9689846?hl=en]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C020`](../sessions/D2-S02-welcome-to-indexing-day.md) Slide, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google answered on a Q&A slide that it does not treat a robots.txt disallow as a noindex because some extremely important sites disallow their most important pages, by accident or out of ignorance. `[D2-C020, slide, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C844`](../sessions/D2-S02-welcome-to-indexing-day.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google illustrated why it does not treat a robots.txt disallow as noindex with an extremely important site, such as a national tax authority, that blocks very important PDF files with robots.txt: Google cannot index the PDFs' content but can at least show their URLs in search results. `[D2-C844, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C062`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Slide, Day 2, not in Google docs: A slide named internal admin pages, temporary landing pages and thin content as typical use cases for the noindex rule. `[D2-C062, slide, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C106`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Slide, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: The noindex rule consumes crawl budget, because Google must fetch the page to see it. `[D1-C106, slide, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C061`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Slide, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: The noindex robots rule tells Google not to show the page in search results. `[D2-C061, slide, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C068`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: The robots rule none is equivalent to noindex plus nofollow, so a page that carries it will not show up in Search, provided Google can see the tag. `[D2-C068, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C718`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Not-indexed reasons in the Page indexing report include pages excluded by a noindex rule and 'Alternate page with proper canonical tag'. `[D2-C718, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C108`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Slide, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Removing a robots restriction such as noindex with JavaScript does not work, a slide said. `[D2-C108, slide, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C852`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: When Google finds a noindex rule in a page's HTML, it drops the page without even processing its JavaScript, so a script cannot switch the page back to indexable, John Mueller said. `[D2-C852, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C432`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: The canonical leader of a group should be indexable: it should carry no noindex robots directive, return no error status code and not be blocked in robots.txt. `[D2-C432, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C696`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Index selection applies the negative signals that immediately block indexing: noindex (the likely reading of one unclear word), expired unavailable_after dates, soft 404s, non-canonical duplicates, spam signals and other policies. `[D2-C696, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C697`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Index selection drops a document carrying a noindex rule if it was not already dropped earlier in processing (noindex is a likely but not certain reading of the transcript, supported by the later mention of noindex among the Page indexing report reasons). `[D2-C697, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C639`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: After Google processes a page that now returns a 404 or a noindex, it usually removes the page from its serving index within one to three weeks, sometimes much sooner. `[D3-C639, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 3]`
- [`D2-C019`](../sessions/D2-S02-welcome-to-indexing-day.md) Slide, Day 2, nothing to verify: An audience member noted that a robots.txt block does not mean noindex and that explaining this to developers is a constant struggle, and asked why Google does not treat a robots.txt block as a noindex. `[D2-C019, slide, an audience member, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C110`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Analysis: A URL blocked in robots.txt can still be indexed without its content if other pages link to it, and Google cannot see a noindex on a page it is not allowed to fetch. `[D1-C110, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C023`](../sessions/D2-S02-welcome-to-indexing-day.md) Analysis: Explain robots.txt and noindex to developers as two separate controls: robots.txt controls crawling, noindex controls indexing. To keep a page out of Search, let Google crawl it and serve noindex; a robots.txt disallow alone can leave the bare URL in results. `[D2-C023, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C849`](../sessions/D2-S02-welcome-to-indexing-day.md) Analysis: Google's robots.txt introduction names links from elsewhere on the web as the reason a disallowed URL can still be indexed, while on stage Google spoke of the URL's importance; either way, well-linked important URLs are the disallowed ones most likely to appear in results, so keep such pages crawlable with noindex if they must stay out of Search. `[D2-C849, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C109`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Analysis: Ship robots rules in the HTML the server sends and never rely on JavaScript to lift a noindex: Google may skip rendering a page that arrives with noindex, so the page can stay out of the index even if a script removes the tag later. `[D2-C109, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C855`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Analysis: On stage the rule was absolute (Google won't even process the JavaScript of a page served with noindex), while Google's guide says only that it may skip rendering; either way, a noindex in the served HTML must never be one that JavaScript is expected to lift. `[D2-C855, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C193`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Analysis: In a single-page app, let the server return 404 for unknown routes where possible; otherwise use one of the two client-side fixes Google documents for error views: a JavaScript redirect to a URL that returns 404, or a robots noindex added with JavaScript. `[D2-C193, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C530`](../sessions/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) Analysis: Hiding an image as a CSS background is a fragile way to keep it out of Google: it only stops extraction from that page, so the same image URL used in an img element elsewhere or listed in a sitemap can still be indexed; the documented robots.txt or noindex X-Robots-Tag methods are the reliable route. `[D2-C530, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C653`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Analysis: To hide a URL from Google Search urgently, use the Removals tool in Search Console (about 2 hours) and also add a noindex or a 404, which takes one to three weeks to drop the page from the index. `[D3-C653, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-CAN-04` **MUST** · Documented: Point every canonical directly at a final URL that returns 200, is indexable and is linked (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-ERR-02` **MUST** · Documented: Return a real 404 for unknown routes in single-page apps, or use a documented client-side fallback (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-IDX-01` **MUST** · Documented: Use noindex to keep a page out of Search, and leave that URL crawlable (6 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-IDX-02` **AVOID** · Documented: Do not use noindex, nofollow or crawl-delay to save crawl budget (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-IDX-13` **SHOULD** · Documented: For an urgent removal, use the Removals tool in Search Console and also return 404 or noindex (3 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-IMG-06` **SHOULD** · Documented: Keep images out of Search with robots.txt or X-Robots-Tag, not with CSS tricks (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-MON-10` **SHOULD** · Documented: Plan releases and fixes around Google's processing times, and judge results only after them (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-REN-05` **AVOID** · Documented: Do not add, change or remove robots meta tags with JavaScript (4 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
